column1: # Highest points where Wikidata needs a choice.

column4: Wikidata gives two peaks of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Pico Cristóbal Colón and Pico Simón Bolívar, whose heights have not been told apart by survey (Wikipedia): left out
the highest ground is an unnamed spot on Villingili (Wikidata gives Villingili and Addu City, Wikipedia "an unnamed location on Villingili, 5.1 m"): no named point, left out
Wikidata gives Velika Rudoka (2658 m), which is in Kosovo; Kosovo is its own row here, so Serbia's is Midžor, as Wikipedia's list of elevation extremes gives it
Wikidata gives Mawson Peak (2745 m) on Heard Island, an external territory far in the Southern Ocean; Wikipedia's list and the usual answer are Mount Kosciuszko, the highest on the continent
Halti's summit (1361 m, Wikidata's height) is in Norway; Finland's highest point is on its slope at 1324 m (Wikipedia's list)
Roraima's summit (2810 m, Wikidata's height) is not in Guyana; Guyana's highest point on it is 2772 m (Wikipedia's list)
Jebel Jais's summit is in Oman; the UAE's highest point on it is 1892 m (Wikipedia's list; Wikidata 1911)
Wikidata gives Mowdok Tiang (1054 m), Wikipedia's list Saka Haphong (1063 m): the sources disagree, left out
Wikidata gives Mount Afadja (885 m), Wikipedia's list Leklata (900 m): the sources disagree, left out
Wikidata gives Monte Torin (262 m), Wikipedia's list Dongol Rondè (266 m): the sources disagree, left out
Wikidata gives Mutla Ridge (140 m), Wikipedia's list an unnamed place in the far west (291 m): left out
Wikidata gives the Népin cliff (531 m), Wikipedia's list Felo Barkere (638 m): the sources disagree, left out
Wikidata gives Dolohmwar (791 m), Wikipedia's list Nanlaud (782 m): the sources disagree, left out
Wikidata names Kibo, the summit cone of Kilimanjaro (5895 m); Wikipedia's list and the usual name are Kilimanjaro
